web_title: 6. Multi-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Chapter 6: Forensic Audit of the Books — Cash Conversion & Capital Efficiency
question: Do IGIL's multi-year income statement, cash flows, and balance sheet confirm high-quality compounding, or are there hidden distortions from the 2024 roll-up?

epigraph.quote: Accounting profit is an opinion; cash from operations divided by EBITDA is a lie detector.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.title: Multi-year P&L trajectory and quarterly acceleration

web_blocks.html: IGIL's consolidated financial path reflects both organic scaling and the December 2024 global consolidation. Annual sales rose from ₹491 Cr in CY2022 to ₹898 Cr in CY2023 (+83% YoY) and ₹1,053 Cr in CY2024 (+17% YoY). Sales reached ₹1,598 Cr across the 15-month transition period ended March 2026 [1]. On a trailing twelve-month (TTM) basis through September 2026, revenue stands at ₹1,457 Cr (+24% YoY). TTM operating profit is ₹896 Cr (61% OPM) and net profit is ₹666 Cr [1]. Quarterly revenue rose steadily from ₹265 Cr in Dec 2024 to ₹398 Cr in Sep 2026 (+31% YoY). Quarterly net profit climbed from ₹114 Cr to ₹186 Cr (+43% YoY) over the same span [1, 5].

web_blocks.caption: IGIL Consolidated Profit & Loss Trajectory (CY2022 – TTM Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Operating margins expanded from 55% in CY2023 to 61% in 15M FY26 and TTM Sep 2026, demonstrating strong fixed-cost leverage across global labs.

web_blocks.caption: IGIL Quarterly Performance Progression (Dec 2024 – Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: YoY sales growth accelerated for five consecutive quarters from +6% in Dec 2024 to +31% in Sep 2026 following GIA's October 2025 LGD grading shift.

web_blocks.html: The quarterly progression highlights an unmistakable inflection after October 2025. YoY sales growth stepped up for five straight quarters, rising from +6% in Dec 2024 to +31% in Sep 2026 [1, 5]. Over the same span, quarterly net profit grew from ₹114 Cr to ₹186 Cr, a +43% YoY jump in Q2 FY27 [1, 5]. Fixed lab staffing and equipment costs stayed controlled as volumes scaled, lifting operating margins to 61% [1].

web_blocks.title: Balance sheet transformation, debt profile, and capital efficiency

web_blocks.html: Reading IGIL's balance sheet requires separating pre-IPO restructuring noise from post-IPO reality. In Dec 2023, reserves dropped to -₹605 Cr and other liabilities spiked to ₹1,484 Cr due to common-control accounting and pre-IPO promoter restructuring [1]. Following the December 2024 equity raise and the $158.2 million purchase of IGI Belgium and IGI Netherlands, equity capital rose to ₹86 Cr. Reserves rebuilt to ₹976 Cr in Dec 2024, ₹1,402 Cr in Mar 2026, and ₹1,665 Cr by Sep 2026 [1]. Total borrowings stand at just ₹150 Cr, mostly lease liabilities under Ind AS 116, against ₹1,751 Cr of shareholders' equity. The business is effectively net debt-free, earning 69.2% ROCE and 55.8% ROE [1].

web_blocks.caption: IGIL Consolidated Balance Sheet Structure (CY2022 – Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Post-IPO reserves grew from ₹976 Cr (Dec 2024) to ₹1,665 Cr (Sep 2026) while borrowings remained flat at ₹150 Cr, confirming self-funded expansion.

web_blocks.title: Cash conversion and working capital forensics

web_blocks.html: Cash conversion is the strongest forensic check on IGIL's earnings quality. Pre-tax CFO/EBITDA conversion held at 87% in CY2022, 90% in CY2023, 91% in CY2024, and 94% in 15M FY26. Nearly every rupee of reported operating profit became real cash [1]. Free cash flow compounded from ₹183 Cr in CY2022 to ₹248 Cr in CY2023, ₹355 Cr in CY2024, and ₹543 Cr in 15M FY26 [1]. The ₹1,634 Cr investing outflow in CY2024 and ₹320 Cr outflow in 15M FY26 reflect the Belgium/Netherlands consolidation and the AGL buyout, not maintenance capex.

web_blocks.caption: IGIL Consolidated Cash Flow & Free Cash Flow Conversion (CY2022 – 15M FY26, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Pre-tax CFO/EBITDA conversion improved every year from 87% to 94%, generating ₹543 Cr of free cash flow in 15M FY26.

web_blocks.caption: IGIL Working Capital & Efficiency Ratios (CY2022 – 15M FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: Debtor days rose from 47 to 66 days over four periods, making receivables collection the primary forensic item to monitor.

web_blocks.html: The working-capital ratios confirm strong cash discipline with one clear watchpoint. Inventory stays negligible because IGIL grades customer stones on consignment and holds only master reference stones [15]. Debtor days, however, drifted from 47 days in CY2022 to 66 days in 15M FY26 as large retail chains took longer credit terms [1]. The ₹662M receivables release in Q2 FY27 reversed part of that buildup, keeping cash conversion healthy [15].

web_blocks.text: Balance Sheet Purity, Cash Conversion & Capital Allocation

web_blocks.html: After the December 2024 IPO and Belgium/Netherlands buyout, IGIL runs with a nearly debt-free balance sheet and substantial net cash. Debt/Equity sits at 0.09x, driven mostly by lease liabilities under Ind AS 116 [1][4]. Pre-tax CFO/EBITDA conversion stayed between 87% and 94% from CY22 through 15M FY26. That consistency confirms that 57%–61% operating margins reflect real cash collections rather than aggressive revenue booking [1][3]. With capex below 4% of revenue, excess cash easily funds bolt-on deals like AGL ($13.2M) and regular dividends [1][8].

IGIL's 69.2% ROCE and 55.8% ROE reflect an asset-light model where net fixed assets—mostly lab equipment and leased premises—turn over multiple times each year [1]. Effective tax rates normalize near 25%–26% across India, Belgium, and the US. With maintenance capex under 4% of sales, IGIL's incremental return on invested capital ranks among the highest in the Indian mid-cap universe [1][3].
IGIL's 10-year financial record pairs software-like margins with low fixed-asset intensity. The result is strong cash conversion across every industry transition [1][3].

book_paragraphs: A high-margin service business should leave unmistakable footprints in its cash flow statement. If profits are real, operating cash flow tracks operating profit closely, debt stays negligible, and equity compounds without repeated capital calls. IGIL passes that forensic test with room to spare.

Across its audited history, revenue scaled from ₹491 Cr in CY2022 to ₹1,053 Cr in CY2024 and ₹1,598 Cr in the 15-month transition period ended March 2026. On a trailing twelve-month basis through September 2026, sales reached ₹1,457 Cr with operating profit of ₹896 Cr—a 61% operating margin—and net profit of ₹666 Cr. Even more importantly, pre-tax operating cash flow converted 87% to 94% of operating EBITDA in every single reported period, generating ₹355 Cr of free cash flow in CY2024 and ₹543 Cr in 15M FY26.

book_subsections.title: Cleaning the Balance Sheet Noise and Checking Credit Quality
paragraphs: At first glance, the December 2023 balance sheet looks alarming, with reserves at -₹605 Cr and other liabilities at ₹1,484 Cr. That anomaly reflects pre-IPO common-control restructuring obligations before the December 2024 listing. Once fresh IPO proceeds paid for IGI Belgium and IGI Netherlands, the balance sheet snapped into clean alignment: by September 2026, shareholders' equity reached ₹1,751 Cr (₹86 Cr share capital plus ₹1,665 Cr reserves) against just ₹150 Cr of total borrowings, yielding a 69.2% return on capital employed and a 55.8% return on equity.

The one forensic yellow flag is the steady rise in debtor days from 47 days in CY2022 to 66 days in 15M FY26. While Q2 FY27 reversed part of that buildup with a ₹662 million receivables release, owners should continue auditing collection velocity in upcoming annual reports to verify that fast top-line growth is not being subsidized by looser credit to diamond cutters.

book_subsections.title: Separating Real Compounding from Accounting Optics
paragraphs: Let us put the financial statements under a forensic microscope. When a company reports 69.2% ROCE and 55.8% ROE alongside ~60% operating margins, your first instinct as a skeptic should be: is this real, or is it an artifact of low book equity or aggressive capitalization? Here, the cash flow statement settles the debate. Across every audited period from CY22 through the 15-month FY26 transition, pre-tax operating cash flow tracked 87% to 94% of EBITDA. There is no capitalized R&D hiding expenses, no bloated goodwill-to-assets trap outside the cleanly disclosed Belgium/Netherlands/AGL consolidations, and virtually zero financial leverage.

The only nuance you must account for when comparing historical periods is the fiscal-year transition. Because IGIL shifted from a December calendar year to a March fiscal year via a 15-month period ending March 31, 2026 (₹15,976M revenue), naive trailing-twelve-month comparisons can distort growth rates unless you normalize to quarterly YoY run-rates. On a clean YoY basis, Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹398.0 Cr (+31% YoY) and PAT of ₹185.8 Cr (+43% YoY) confirm that the core compounding engine is accelerating, not decelerating.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: THE MPS OVERHANG WATCHPOINT
callouts.text: Clean cash flows do not eliminate structural share-supply risk. Blackstone still holds 76.55% as promoter, which means at least 1.55%—and potentially much larger private-equity blocks—must come to market before December 2027 to satisfy SEBI's 75% Minimum Public Shareholding rule.

book_subsections.title: Reading the 15-Month Transition & Tax Normalization
paragraphs: Whenever a company changes its fiscal calendar, careless analysts misread the year-on-year growth table. IGIL shifted from a December year-end to an Indian March fiscal year via a 15-month period ending March 31, 2026, generating ₹15,976 million in revenue. That is why we anchor our forensic audit to both the audited CY2024 baseline and the clean three-month YoY comparisons in FY27.

Strip out the calendar noise, and the financial quality is unmistakable. Debt-to-equity sits at 0.09 times—almost entirely Ind AS 116 lease liabilities on laboratory premises rather than bank borrowings. Cash conversion remains elite, capex is under 4% of revenue, and management has already shown it can fund tuck-in M&A like AGL's $13.2 million deal purely from internal accruals while paying a 0.58% dividend.

book_subsections.title: Cash Generation, Dividend Discipline & Return on Incremental Capital
paragraphs: Put yourself in the seat of a capital allocator looking at IGIL's balance sheet. After funding the $158.2 million Belgium and Netherlands consolidation out of IPO proceeds and paying $13.2 million in cash for AGL, IGIL still carries virtually zero bank debt and generates over ₹33 of free cash flow for every ₹100 of revenue.

Because opening a new satellite lab or adding optical spectrometers requires minimal fixed capital, IGIL does not need to retain 100% of its earnings to fund 20%-plus growth. That is why the company can simultaneously invest in new capacity, fund selective bolt-on acquisitions in colored stones or digital provenance tools, and still return cash to shareholders via regular dividends while compounding ROCE near 69%.

book_subsections.title: Forensic Checklist Summary: Zero Red Flags, Two Clear Watchpoints
paragraphs: Let us close our financial forensics chapter with a clean scorecard. Cash conversion? Elite at 87% to 94% of EBITDA. Leverage? Virtually zero bank debt, with Debt/Equity at 0.09x from office leases. Capital intensity? Under 4% of revenue. Return on capital? 69.2% ROCE and 55.8% ROE.

The only two items on our forensic watch-list are receivables discipline—where debtor days rose to 66 by March 2026 before Q2 FY27's ₹662 million collection release—and the upcoming December 2027 SEBI Minimum Public Shareholding reduction by Blackstone. Neither undermines the integrity of the historical earnings.

book_callouts.title: What This Means for an Owner
book_callouts.text: IGIL exhibits elite financial forensics: 61% operating margins, 94% pre-tax CFO/EBITDA conversion, negligible debt, and 69.2% ROCE. Its business quality earns a COMPOUNDER_PASS on price-blind fundamentals.
